```{r connect-db, include=FALSE}
# Reconnect to the course DuckDB repository built from the Week 1 Part 3 notes.

public_example <- readRDS("~/RBIF111/database/public_example.rds")

                   GB = cfg$DuckDB_GB,
                   ReadOnly = TRUE)
```

# Question 1

## 1.1 A loop-based mean function

```{r q1-function}
my_mean <- function(x, na.rm = FALSE) {
  if (na.rm == TRUE) {
    x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  }
  total <- 0
  for (i in 1:length(x)) {
    total <- total + x[i]
  }
  total / length(x)
}
```

**How the code works:**

The function starts a running total at 0. The for loop visits each position in the vector and adds the value x[i] to the total. At the end it divides the total by length(x), the number of values.

```{r q1-compare}
v <- c(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42)
my_mean(v)
mean(v)
```

**Interpretation:**
Both `my_mean(v)` and `mean(v)` returned 18, so my loop-based function gives the same answer as R's built-in `mean()`.

## 1.2 Handling NA values

```{r q1-na}
v_na <- c(4, NA, 15, 16, NA, 42)

my_mean(v_na)
mean(v_na)

my_mean(v_na, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(v_na, na.rm = TRUE)
```

**How the NA handling works:**

When `na.rm = TRUE`, the line `x <- x[!is.na(x)]` removes the missing values (the NAs) before the loop runs, so the mean is calculated from only the remaining numbers. In my example, `c(4, NA, 15, 16, NA, 42)` becomes `c(4, 15, 16, 42)`, which has 4 values. When `na.rm = FALSE`, the NAs stay in the vector, so the loop adds an NA into the total. In R, any number plus NA is NA, so the function returns `NA`. This matches how R's `mean()` works, because the true mean cannot be known if some values are missing.


**Why the loop-based function and mean() are expected to agree:**

My function and `mean()` are expected to agree because they use the same definition of a mean: add up all the values and divide by the number of values. My function just does the adding one value at a time with a loop. Because the math is the same, both give the same answer, as shown above.

```{r q1-find-table}
tabs <- DBI::dbListTables(con)

```

```{r q1-describe}
# Replace NHANES_BMX with the exact table name printed above
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "DESCRIBE NHANES_BMX")
```

Pull the column with SQL and compare:

```{r q1-duckdb-mean}
bmi <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT BMXBMI FROM NHANES_BMX")$BMXBMI
length(bmi)
sum(is.na(bmi))

my_mean(bmi, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(bmi, na.rm = TRUE)
all.equal(my_mean(bmi, na.rm = TRUE), mean(bmi, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## 1.4 Hypothesis test: height vs weight

**Null hypothesis (H0):** There is zero correlation between height and weight in NHANES participants (the true correlation coefficient, r, equals 0).

**Alternative hypothesis (H1):** There is a correlation between height and weight in NHANES participants (the true correlation coefficient, r, is not equal to 0).


```{r q1-cor-all}
hw <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT BMXHT, BMXWT
  FROM NHANES_BMX
  WHERE BMXHT IS NOT NULL AND BMXWT IS NOT NULL")
nrow(hw)

ggplot(hw, aes(BMXHT, BMXWT)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Height (cm)", y = "Weight (kg)",
       title = "NHANES: height vs weight (all ages)")

res_all <- cor.test(hw$BMXHT, hw$BMXWT)
res_all
```

```{r q1-cor-adults}
# Restrict to adults by joining to demographics on SEQN
# Check the real DEMO table name first: grep("DEMO", tabs, value = TRUE)
hw_adults <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT b.BMXHT, b.BMXWT
  FROM NHANES_BMX b
  JOIN NHANES_DEMO d ON b.SEQN = d.SEQN
  WHERE d.RIDAGEYR >= 18
    AND b.BMXHT IS NOT NULL AND b.BMXWT IS NOT NULL")
nrow(hw_adults)

res_adults <- cor.test(hw_adults$BMXHT, hw_adults$BMXWT)
res_adults
```
